title: Refit a pressure cooker's float valve cap: hold the loose valve in from the top and snap the silicone cap on underneath
instruction: Put the silicone cap back on the bottom of the pressure cooker lid's float valve.
context: Owners of electric pressure cookers take the float valve and its silicone cap off the lid to wash them, and must refit them: without the cap the cooker cannot seal. The valve is loose in its hole, so pushing the cap onto its underside end just pushes the valve out of the top, and the maker's guide says to keep a finger on the valve's flat top while attaching the cap.
setup: Cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y left); heights above the table. Dish rack lid slot, fixed, white plastic-coated wire on a pale blue plastic drip tray (30 x 13 x 1.2, centre x 31, y -0.6): a 22 cm bar the lid stands on, top 2.5 high, and two rows of five tines 7 tall at y -2.6 and 1.1, each row joined by a rail 8.2 high. Lid of a 6-quart electric pressure cooker, fixed in the slot: 25 across, standing on edge, its top face toward +y, centre x 31, y 0, 15 high; brushed steel cover over a steel inner lid, 1.2 thick round the valve; rim 2.5 deep; black handle 3.4 x 2.8 x 20 across the top face, vertical through the centre; black steam release knob (2.4 across, 1.8 tall) on the top face at x 35.5, 19.5 high; dark float valve pin lock (0.8 across, 1 tall) on the top face at x 29, 23.5 high; with a steel anti-block shield behind it on the underside; white silicone sealing ring on the underside. Float valve hole, its axis along y, at x 25, y 0, 15 high (6 from the lid's centre, toward the arms). Float valve, loose in its hole: stainless steel, 10 g; flat top 10 mm across, 2.5 mm thick, resting on the top face; 5 mm shank in a 6 mm hole, ending 3 mm below the underside; groove 3.4 mm across, 1.2 mm long; end knob 5.4 mm across, 1.8 mm long, chamfered to 3.2 mm at the tip. Silicone cap, loose, white, 2 g: 12 mm across, 6.5 mm long, closed end; 3.6 mm hole through a 1 mm lip at its open end (mouth chamfered to 4.8 mm), 6 mm bore behind it; lying open side down on the table at x 20, y -12. Distractors (scoring ignores them): dish soap bottle, clear plastic with green liquid and cap, 27 tall, 400 g, upright at x 47, y 22; red ceramic mug, 8 tall, 320 g, upright at x 47, y -21; kitchen sponge, green scourer on yellow foam, 7 x 10 x 3.3, 20 g, flat at x 13, y 23.
scoring: Measured on the lid with a ruler and a 0.6 mm feeler gauge (or three sheets of printer paper): in a real trial, seated means the cap's face is tight against the step at the shank's end, the gauge not entering between them, and the cap square on the valve. Seated: the cap's open face within 0.6 mm short of or 0.4 mm past the end of the valve's shank (its lip in the groove, the end knob past it), the cap's axis within 10 deg and 0.6 mm of the valve's. Fell out: the valve pushed more than 10 mm out of the lid's top face at any time before full credit (a real valve drops out there). Hands clear: every gripper fingertip at least 2 cm from both the cap and the valve's top. 1.0 once the cap has been seated, still (under 1 cm/s) and hands clear for 1 s running, with the valve never fallen out; then kept. 0 if the valve fell out, whatever follows. Otherwise, at the end of the run: 0.25 if the cap is left on the valve's end but not seated (open face from 3 mm short of the shank's end to 0.4 mm past it, axis within 30 deg and 1.5 mm), still and hands clear; 0 for anything else (cap on the table or elsewhere, or still held).
reset_notes: Pull the cap off the valve, stand the lid back in the rack slot (in a real trial the lid is clamped in the slot so it cannot rock), push the valve back down so its flat top rests on the lid, and lay the cap open side down at its mark (tape marks on the counter). Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Valve, cap and lid at real size; the cooker base is not in the scene and the lid is fixed in the rack slot. Rigid bodies: the cap lip's stretch is modelled as the valve's end knob in four sprung quarters that give inward (150 N/m each), so the cap goes on with about 1 N, less than a real one. The valve slides freely in its hole; past 10 mm out it counts as fallen out (the simulated one stops at 12 mm). No steam or pressure. Friction about 0.15 on wet steel, 0.9 on silicone.
